concepts.def: Bar graph of age-sex structure; pyramids show youthful populations (Nigeria), inverted shapes show ageing (Japan).
Five stages tracking birth/death rates with development; UK reached Stage 4 in 20th century.
Ratio of dependents (under 15 and over 65) to working-age population; higher ratio means more economic burden.
Rising median age and over-65 share; Japan 29% over 65; strains pensions, healthcare; resolved by immigration or pro-natalism.
Voluntary for economic/lifestyle reasons (EU workers to UK); forced by conflict, persecution, disaster (Syrian refugees).
Difference between immigration and emigration; positive means population gain; UK net migration around 600,000 (2023).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Population & Migration — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Population & Migration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Population & Migration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What does a wide-based pyramid show?

numericals.q: How many stages in the Demographic Transition Model?

free_texts.hint: Higher number means more economic burden.
